defect_1_fabricated_rule_clause.original_rule_text: enrolled_in(Medicare | Medicaid | TRICARE | VA | DOD | any_federal_or_state_healthcare_program) => NOT ELIGIBLE for commercial savings card, including when the beneficiary offers to pay cash
defect_1_fabricated_rule_clause.problem: The trailing clause 'including when the beneficiary offers to pay cash' appears in NO located source. The original run correctly recorded that no verbatim quote was obtained, then authored a rule containing an invented provision. An unsupported clause in a legal-eligibility rule is a fabrication regardless of whether it happens to be true of real copay-card terms.
defect_1_fabricated_rule_clause.remedy: Strike the clause. Keep only predicates that located text supports.

defect_3_pap_wegovy_coverage_framed_as_u.original_claim: whether EITHER Wegovy formulation is covered by PAP at all was never established
defect_3_pap_wegovy_coverage_framed_as_u.located_evidence: PAP covers insulins, Ozempic, Rybelsus, Victoza. Wegovy and Saxenda are NOT currently covered.
defect_3_pap_wegovy_coverage_framed_as_u.problem: This is a located POSITIVE EXCLUSION, not an unknown. Framing it as unknown leaves open the possibility that a downstream build offers a PAP pathway for Wegovy. A patient would be routed to apply for a program that does not cover their drug.
defect_3_pap_wegovy_coverage_framed_as_u.remedy: Encode as 'located: Wegovy not a PAP covered product', confidence unverified, value null.

defect_4_fpl_two_tier_confirmed_as_locat.located: Household income at or below 200% FPL for Ozempic; at or below 400% FPL for all other medications. Patients must be uninsured or have Medicare; private/commercial insurance disqualifies.
defect_4_fpl_two_tier_confirmed_as_locat.assessment: The original run's two-tier reading is corroborated by secondary sources. Its objection to the task's single-threshold premise is well founded. No defect here.

verbatim_excerpt: You are not eligible for a savings card if you do not have commercial drug insurance or if you are enrolled in any state, federal, or government-funded healthcare program, including, without limitation, Medicaid, Medicare, Medicare Part D, Medicare Advantage, Medigap, DoD, VA, TRICARE CHAMPUS, or any state healthcare program. ... The maximum savings are $100 per 1-month prescription, $200 per 2-month prescription, or $300 per 3-month prescription. ... Total household income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level for Ozempic. For all other medications, total household income must be at or below 400% of the federal poverty level. ... The PAP primarily covers diabetes medications such as insulin, Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Victoza. Wegovy and Saxenda are not currently covered.
